data.name: Roseline
data.gender_notes: Roseline is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word rosa, meaning 'rose', and linum, meaning 'linen'. Roses symbolize love, beauty, and grace. Linen is a fabric made from flax fibers. In Christianity, roses can represent the Virgin Mary or the Resurrection of Jesus. The name Roseline carries the meaning “Rose, Linen” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Roseline usually hope their child will grow to embody rose, linen and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of divine love and grace.
data.etymology: Roseline belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Rose, Linen.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Roseline total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.
data.cultural_impact: The name "Roseline" may evoke thoughts of beauty, elegance, and romance due to the symbolism of roses in Western culture. It may also be reminiscent of the Medieval practice of giving a rosed garland (rosary) as a symbol of love and devotion.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Christian context, the name "Roseline" can symbolize a deep connection with spirituality and the divine, drawing from the symbolism of the rose in religious traditions. It may represent devotion to the Virgin Mary, who is often depicted holding a rose or roses, or serve as a reminder of the hope and renewal associated with the Resurrection of Jesus, symbolized by the rose.

historical_references.reference: Roseline of Limoges, a 13th-century French saint, was known for her piety and her care for the sick.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Roseline remains relevant in modern Christian society, representing a bridge between traditional Biblical values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Ruth Roseline in Jerusalem, Israel credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Roseline, which means "Rose, Linen". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.
